PocketBudJet opens with a splash after you install. Wait for it to finish, then continue.
Swipe the welcome slides. With PocketBudJet you can run envelopes, bills, and goals on your phone.
You also get a coach that flags unusual spending.
If you'd like, watch loan progress and your debt-free date on this tour.
Your numbers stay on your phone. Tap Get Started.
On first launch, the Terms tab is open. Scroll to the bottom.
Disclaimer is the other tab. Scroll that one to the bottom too.
When both tabs are done, tap I Accept — Continue.
On Secure Your Data, turn on app lock if you want a PIN or Face.
You land on Home. Income, spending, and net sit in the big card at the top.
First time in, a short tour pops up. Down here is the tab bar — Home, Activity, Budget, Goals, and Coach.
Search and Coach sit up top too. You'll see them on every screen.
Swipe in from the left. Settings, Help, and the whole map come out.
Toolbox is import, scan, and extras in one place.
The plus button adds a transaction, category, or goal depending on the tab.
On your second open — or after five transactions — you may see Choose Your Plan. Start the 15-day Premium trial with no card, or stay free.
PocketBudJet may ask to send bill reminders. Allow notifications if you want a heads-up before due dates.
Setup is optional. If you'd like the wizard, tap the gear, open Settings, then tap Set Up PocketBudJet.
This is the name that shows on Home. Type it in and tap Next.
Home will use this currency. Pick yours and keep going.
Accounts are optional — checking, savings, credit, or cash. Skip if you'd rather add them later.
Income is what fills the hero card. Enter gross and take-home — you can itemize the rest later.
If you'd like, add the bills that come every month — name, amount, due day. Or skip and come back.
A main money goal helps Home personalize. Pick one if it fits.

On Budget Template, pick the style that fits. 50/30/20 is half needs, 30 percent wants, 20 percent savings. Aggressive Saver puts more toward savings. Envelope gives each category a fixed amount. Zero-Based gives every dollar a job so income minus expenses is zero. Tap the one you want, then Apply Template.
There's a color question so the charts stay easy to read. Answer that and continue.
You're looking at the recap. If it looks right, tap Finish — then you're on Home.
Back on Home, the hero card is the glance: income, spending, and net.
This is Activity. When it is empty, tap Add my first transaction — or import a statement and the list fills in.
You might want to import a few months first. Then every charge shows up here, grouped by date.
When you have rows, the filter stacks date, category, and account. Use it to narrow the list.
Open any row later to change the category, split it, add a note, or attach a receipt.
If a share comes in with unsure rows, open Approve Transactions and fix them before they hit your budget.
With PocketBudJet you can set monthly envelopes. Tap Budget on the tab bar — the calendar icon.
Here's Budget after a month is in. Each category has a bar and a limit. Tap a row if you want to change the cap.
On first setup, this list is where you name categories and set the monthly limit.
If you'd like a different style later, tap Change Template. Same four: 50/30/20, Aggressive Saver, Envelope, or Zero-Based.
Category Manager is where you add, merge, or hide a category.
Spending Plan fills in after you have transactions. Add a few months, then come back for your safe-to-spend number.
Savings targets live on Goals. Tap the trending-up icon.
Nothing tracked yet. Here's how: tap Add one under Savings Goals.
Enter a name, a target amount, and a date. PocketBudJet figures the monthly set-aside.
You might want a sinking fund for insurance or a vacation. Same Add one when you are ready.
Purchase Wishlist lets you park a want with a cooling-off timer before the money leaves.
With PocketBudJet you get a Coach on the last tab. Tap Coach — the sparkles.
Here's Today after a month is in. Coach calls out what to watch — groceries, in this case.
If you'd like, tap Ask and talk in plain English. Try How much did I spend on dining last month?
Coach can also send a weekly recap. Same tab, just open it when the notification lands.
To log one charge by hand, tap the gold plus from any screen.
Here's that plus. You can finish in under ten seconds.
Amount first, while the number is fresh.
Type the merchant the same way each time. Then pick a category and the account.
For a mixed receipt, tap Split. Put parts in Groceries, Household, or whatever fits — the total stays locked.
Tap Save. Home and the envelope update right away.
With PocketBudJet you can bring in a bank statement. No bank login needed. Open Toolbox, then tap Import Center.
Share from your bank app is the path. Labels vary by bank. Tap Show me how.
Here's step by step. In your bank app, open Statements. Tap the statement date you want.
Download puts the statement on your phone.
Share it to PocketBudJet. If it is not in the first row, tap More and find it.
Review the list. Tap Import when the rows look right.
Your numbers land on Home. Here's where the money went. Import another statement the same way anytime.
Import History keeps past shares. Tap a row if you want to open one again.
If you'd like to add a paper receipt, tap Scan Receipt and take a photo. Merchant, amount, and date show on the form.
Check the fields, pick a category if you need to, then tap Save.
For a stack of paper, open the document scanner in Toolbox and follow the steps on the screen.
Load the stack. The pages show up on Activity when they are done.
Universal Scan also takes statements and invoices. Crop the corners, review, then import.
On Bills, the calendar shows due dates and payday marks.
Add Bill is for a subscription or a recurring payment. A due date can mark it paid or snooze the reminder.
Subscription Tracker lists repeating charges you might have forgotten.
Recurring Transactions puts bills and income on one timeline.
Recurring Income is where paychecks and side gigs live, so forecasts know when money arrives.
You can import or photograph a pay stub. Pay Stub Review splits gross, taxes, and deductions.
Direct Deposit Advisor suggests how to split a paycheck across accounts and envelopes.
On Debt, enter balances, APR, and minimum payments.
Pick avalanche — highest interest first — or snowball — smallest balance first. You'll see a debt-free date.
Loan Calculator lets you try extra payments or a refinance before you commit.
Debt Progress charts how fast balances are falling month over month.
In Coach, tap Reports for spending by category, income versus expenses, and layouts you save.
Spending Trends compares month to month. Spot a seasonal spike before it becomes a habit.
Category Breakdown shows where the money went. Share a CSV or PDF from the share icon if you want a copy.
Merchant Analysis ranks stores by spend — handy for cutting dining or a subscription.
Financial Health Score grades savings rate, debt, and whether you stayed in budget — one number.
Report Builder lets you save a filter and reuse it for the monthly review.
Net Worth tracks accounts, investments, property, and what you owe, in one view.
In Settings, open How PocketBudJet Learns. Correct a category once and later rows follow. Your numbers stay on your phone.
Bank sync is for US banks on paid Premium — not in the free trial. Two banks are included. Tap Connect to begin.
In Settings, tap Connect Bank. Search for your US bank and sign in. PocketBudJet never stores your bank password.
Tax Filing Export bundles categories and mileage for your accountant or tax software.
Tax Center groups mileage, deductions, and the year summary.
Mileage Log tracks business miles. Start a trip from Toolbox or a widget.
Deduction Breakdown totals the tax-prep categories from the rows you already categorized.
The gear is Settings — accounts, privacy, backups, and the setup wizard.
My Profile and Accounts is where you change the display name and account types.
If you'd like to share a budget with a partner, Household sync walks the invite on each phone.
In Privacy and Backup, tap Backup to turn on encrypted cloud backup and app lock.
Under Data Management, tap Storage to decide how much history stays on the phone.
How PocketBudJet Learns again: correct a category, and later rows follow. Your numbers stay on your phone.
Bank sync is US banks on paid Premium — not in the 15-day trial. Two banks included; extras are an add-on. Tap Connect.
Search for your US bank and sign in. PocketBudJet never stores your bank password.
Choose checking, savings, or credit to link. New transactions show up and follow your rules.
Open Activity, tap a transaction, then Transaction Rules. Here's how you automate a repeat merchant.
Example: when the name contains Coffee Shop, assign Dining. Future imports pick that up.
Flag an odd row with Bookmarks. Filter Activity to bookmarks only when you reconcile.
You might want hands-free entry. Say Hey Siri, log 12 dollars coffee in PocketBudJet — or use a Google Assistant shortcut.
Ask How much is left in Groceries, or What's my net worth. Voice works for budgets and Coach.
Retirement Planning asks for a target age, yearly spend, and what you have saved. Tap Target Retirement Age, then fill the rest.
Couples Dashboard shows shared envelopes and who spent what. Each phone still keeps its own copy.
In Settings, open Purchase Wishlist. Tap Add Item to cool off before a big buy — thirty days is a good test.
Shopping Intelligence compares prices and flags a pattern at checkout.
Launch PC Web Companion from Toolbox. When it is running, scan the QR or open the link on a PC on the same Wi-Fi.
If you'd like, turn on Notification Capture in Settings. A bank alert can become a draft transaction.
Couples Dashboard again: shared envelopes, who spent what, still stored on each phone.
Search is in the header. Find a charge by merchant or amount — or a feature like mileage.
Connect Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, or iCloud for encrypted backup. Your cloud, your control.
Notification Capture can turn a bank alert into a draft. Opt in from Settings if you want it.
Widgets and Watch can show safe-to-spend, bills due, and quick-add. Set the slots in Settings.
In Settings under Data and Privacy, tap Require app unlock if you want Face or a passcode before numbers appear.
Same backup step if you skipped it: Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, or iCloud. Your account, your control.
Need help? Email support@josspatech.com or use in-app feedback. This guide is at josspatech.com/videos/pbj/user-guide.
